standard_prerequisites.name: Kac chaos set-up and canonical tensor product
standard_prerequisites.statement: A symmetric mu_N in P(O^N) is p-chaotic if every k-particle marginal P_k mu_N converges weakly to p^{otimes k}; gamma(p,rho_N) is p^{otimes N} conditioned on Omega_{rho_N} and gamma_N(p) = gamma(p,rho^pi_N).
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the objects compared in the two displays.

standard_prerequisites.name: Multivariate CLT normalisation on the induced measure space
standard_prerequisites.statement: S_N = sum_{j<=N} xi(j) in {0,...,N}^K, with covariance V_1, nondegenerate when det V_1 != 0 and irreducible when every coordinate can be flipped with positive probability.
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies K, V_1 and the admissible sequence convention; no rate is assumed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Local CLT normalisation corollary
standard_prerequisites.statement: If mu is irreducible and the admissible sequence satisfies <rho_N - pi, rho_N - pi> = O(1/N), then mu^{otimes N}(Omega_{rho_N}) >= c N^{-K/2} for large N.
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the positive lower bound for the denominator of the Fourier quotient at line 634; the corollary itself is a consequence of the local CLT proved later in the paper.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exponential decay of the characteristic function
standard_prerequisites.reference: source 546-552, with its complete proof at 555-583
standard_prerequisites.statement: For irreducible mu there is c = c(mu) > 0 with |psi(t)| <= exp(-c<t,t>) on [-pi,pi]^K.
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the far part of the Fourier integral into a Gaussian-type weight exp(-a<s,s>/N).

core_obligations: Write the conditioned expectation gamma_N(f) - mu_N(f) as the Fourier quotient (eq:chao5) over Q_{N,K} after the change of variables s = V_N^{1/2} t and B_N = N^{K/2} sqrt(det V_1) (source 611-634).

Use the lower bound on mu_N(Omega_{rho_N}) from coro2 to reduce (eq:chaos00) to the numerator bounds (eq:chao6) and (eq:chao7), then close them with |psi_N(s)| <= exp(-a<s,s>/N), N-k >= N/2, Schwarz and the explicit second moment k^2<V_1^{-1/2}s, pi-rho_N>^2 + k<s,s> <= Ck<s,s> (635-656).

For the canonical sequence use <pi-rho^pi_N, pi-rho^pi_N> = O(1/N^2) and replace f by f-g with g = (1/k)<V_1^{-1}v, S_k>, v = mu_N(f; S_k), so that the linear term vanishes identically and only a second-order remainder survives (658-700).
Prove the fourth-moment estimate mu_N(<V_1^{-1/2}s, S_k>^4) <= Ck^2<s,s>^2 needed for the k/N rate, reducing it to the centred sums and the leading pair terms of order k^2 (702-716).

proof_roadmap.step: Expand mu_N(Omega_{rho_N}) and mu_N(f 1_{Omega_{rho_N}}) by Fourier inversion, pass to the quotient, and bound the numerator by C|f|_inf k/sqrt(N) using the exponential characteristic-function bound and the covariance identity for S_k.
For rho_N = rho^pi_N subtract the linear approximation g of f, use gamma_N(g) = 0 and the O(1/N^2) closeness of rho^pi_N to pi to reach the k/N rate, controlling the remaining term |mu_N(g)|.
Establish the fourth-moment bound that the second-order remainder needs.

difficulty_reason: The claim carries two different total-variation rates for the same object - Ck/sqrt(N) for an arbitrary admissible sequence and Ck/N for the canonical sequence rho^pi_N - so the proof cannot stop at an asymptotic local CLT. It inverts the Fourier transform of the measure conditioned on Omega_{rho_N} and works with the quotient (eq:chao5) of two such integrals, using the exponential bound |psi_N(s)| <= exp(-a<s,s>/N) from the irreducibility lemma to dominate the denominator and the far region (source 626-642), and then needs the exact second moment k^2<V_1^{-1/2}s, pi-rho_N>^2 + k<s,s> together with the assumption <pi-rho_N, pi-rho_N> = O(1/N) to reach Ck/sqrt(N) (643-656). The sharper k/N display is not a rescaling of the first: it subtracts the linear approximation g = (1/k)<V_1^{-1}v, S_k> so that the first-order term vanishes identically (662-668), uses the O(1/N^2) accuracy of the canonical sequence twice (line 658 and (eq:chaoap1)), and still has to prove a fourth-moment bound of order k^2 (702-716).

compared.actual_statement: source 375-389: particle-number-uniform modified logarithmic Sobolev / entropy-production bounds for strictly separating generalized random transpositions
compared.difference: That item bounds entropy production uniformly in the particle number; the new claim compares the k-particle marginals of a conditioned product measure with p^{otimes k} in total variation, with no entropy and no generator. The public index has no local-central-limit entry at all, and the proof 606-717 shares no span with 375-389.

That card compares two nonlinear recombination solutions with equal one-site marginals (statement 1100-1106, proof 948-1263). The new claim is about a conditioned product measure on the fixed-density shell Omega_{rho_N} and is proved by Fourier inversion; neither statement nor proof spans overlap.

That card proves uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for the finite particle system with an explicit empirical initial error (statement 916-924, proof 948-1870). The new claim is a static equivalence-of-ensembles statement for one conditioned product measure and uses no tree, no Wild expansion and no generator comparison; its proof 606-717 lies outside that card's proof package.
Different paper and different object: a regularity lemma for the limiting nonlinear Markov chain, not a total-variation rate for a conditioned product measure.

editorial_notes: The statement is Theorem th:eqens of Section 2 (Local Central Limit Theorem and Chaos); only this theorem is counted here.

The proof span ends at the closing of its own proof environment at line 717. The immediately following Corollary coro3 at 722-756, which bounds the expected total-variation distance of the empirical measure, is a separate consequence of this theorem and is deliberately not included; the remark at 719-720 explaining the f-g subtraction is also outside the span.

The characteristic-function lemma 546-552 and the normalisation corollary coro2 516-530 are carried as context because the proof invokes them at 634 and 639; their own proofs are not part of this card.
All displayed constants and rates are taken from the fixed publisher source unchanged.
